Beyond the discounts, Veterans Day carries genuine cultural and historical significance. Here are a few things worth knowing about how the day is observed.

"Thank you for your service" has become the standard civilian phrase on Veterans Day — and most veterans appreciate it, even if the sentiment can sometimes feel rote. If you're a civilian reading this guide to understand Veterans Day better, the phrase is appropriate and genuinely well-received by most veterans.

Many Veterans Day ceremonies include a moment of silence or brief ceremony at 11:00 a.m. — honoring the exact hour when the armistice took effect in 1918. National ceremonies at Arlington National Cemetery and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier are among the most significant observances.

The red poppy is the symbol of Memorial Day, not Veterans Day — a common point of confusion. Poppies commemorate fallen soldiers. Veterans Day is about living veterans, which is why the tone is celebratory and grateful rather than somber.
